claims.statement: The manananggal is a mythical creature of Philippine folklore said to detach its upper torso from its lower body; its fangs and wings give it a vampire-like look.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal adalah makhluk mitos dari cerita rakyat Filipina yang konon dapat memisahkan tubuh atasnya dari bagian bawah; taring dan sayapnya membuatnya tampak seperti vampir.
claims.quote: is a mythical creature from the folklore of the Philippines. The creature is said to have the ability to detach and separate its upper torso from the lower part of its body. Its fangs and wings give it a vampire-like appearance.

claims.statement: Manananggál derives from Tagalog tanggál ('to remove', 'to separate'), literally 'remover' or 'separator', interpretable as 'one who separates itself'.
claims.statement_id: Kata manananggál berasal dari kata Tagalog tanggál ('melepas', 'memisahkan'), secara harfiah 'pelepas' atau 'pemisah', dan dapat ditafsirkan 'yang memisahkan dirinya'.
claims.quote: The word manananggál is derived from the Tagalog word tanggál, meaning "to remove" or "to separate", and literally translating to "remover" or "separator". In this case, it may be interpreted as "one who separates itself".

claims.statement: In Philippine folklore the manananggal is usually a fearsome creature, most often female, that separates its upper body, revealing its entrails, and grows large bat-like wings to fly at night in search of victims.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Filipina, manananggal biasanya digambarkan sebagai makhluk menyeramkan, paling sering perempuan, yang memisahkan tubuh atasnya, memperlihatkan isi perut, dan menumbuhkan sayap besar mirip kelelawar untuk terbang mencari korban di malam hari.
claims.quote: In Philippine folklore, the manananggal is typically portrayed as a fearsome and grotesque creature, most often depicted as female. It is known to separate its upper body from its lower half, revealing its entrails and developing large, bat-like wings that allow it to fly at night in search of victims.

claims.statement: The manananggal is believed to prey on sleeping pregnant women with a long proboscis-like tongue to extract fetuses or draw blood.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal dipercaya memangsa perempuan hamil yang tidur dengan lidah panjang seperti belalai untuk mengisap janin atau darah.
claims.quote: The manananggal is commonly believed to prey on sleeping, pregnant women by using an elongated, proboscis-like tongue to extract fetuses or draw blood.

claims.statement: Folklore also links it with newlyweds, lovers and newborns; while it hunts, its lower torso stays motionless and is its weak point, and it is killed by applying salt, garlic, ash or fire to that lower half.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat juga mengaitkannya dengan pengantin baru, kekasih, dan bayi; saat berburu, tubuh bawahnya diam dan menjadi titik lemah, dan cara membunuhnya antara lain menaburkan garam, bawang putih, abu, atau api pada tubuh bawah itu.
claims.quote: Folklore also associates the creature with targeting newlyweds, lovers, newborn children, and occasionally grooms who were abandoned after marriage. During its nocturnal hunt, the creature's severed lower torso remains motionless and is its point of vulnerability. Traditional practices for killing a manananggal include applying salt, garlic, ash, or fire to the lower half

claims.statement: The manananggal myth is widely known in the Visayas, especially Capiz, Iloilo, Bohol and Antique.
claims.statement_id: Mitos manananggal dikenal luas di wilayah Visayas, terutama di Capiz, Iloilo, Bohol, dan Antique.
claims.quote: The myth of the manananggal is widely recognized in the Visayan regions of the Philippines, particularly in the western provinces of Capiz, Iloilo, Bohol, and Antique.

claims.statement: Manananggals are believed to be repelled by garlic, salt and holy water, and to avoid daggers, light, vinegar, spices and a stingray's tail.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal dipercaya dapat diusir dengan bawang putih, garam, dan air suci, dan menghindari belati, cahaya, cuka, rempah, serta ekor ikan pari.
claims.quote: as manananggals are also believed to be repelled by garlic, salt, and holy water. They are also thought to avoid daggers, light, vinegar, spices and the tail of a stingray, which can be fashioned into a whip.

claims.statement: Comparable mythical figures appear in neighbouring Southeast Asian cultures, including Indonesia and Malaysia.
claims.statement_id: Sosok mitos serupa muncul di budaya Asia Tenggara lain, termasuk Indonesia dan Malaysia.
claims.quote: Comparable mythical figures appear in neighboring Southeast Asian cultures, including those of Indonesia and Malaysia.

claims.statement: Plasencia recorded the magtatangal, which showed itself at night to many people without its head or entrails.
claims.statement_id: Plasencia mencatat magtatangal, yang menampakkan diri pada malam hari kepada banyak orang tanpa kepala atau isi perut.
claims.quote: The seventh was called magtatangal, and his purpose was to show himself at night to many persons, without his head or entrails.

claims.statement: Domingo de los Santos's dictionary (1703) says the magtatangal flies and eats human flesh with only half its body, hence its name from tangal, 'to disengage'.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Domingo de los Santos (1703) menulis bahwa magtatangal terbang dan memakan daging manusia hanya dengan separuh tubuhnya, sehingga dinamai dari tangal, 'melepaskan'.
claims.quote: They say that it flies and eats human flesh, but when it flies, it only has half its body, and that is why it is called that because it's tangal which means that it can disengage

claims.statement: Plasencia thought it a fable, though locals said they had seen it; this occurred in Catanduanes.
claims.statement_id: Plasencia menganggapnya dongeng, meski penduduk mengaku melihatnya; ini terjadi di Catanduanes.
claims.quote: This seems to me to be a fable, although the natives affirm that they have seen it, because the devil probably caused them so to believe. This occurred in Catanduanes.

claims.statement: That description is from Fray Domingo de los Santos, Vocabulario de Lengua Tagala (1703).
claims.statement_id: Keterangan itu berasal dari Fray Domingo de los Santos, Vocabulario de Lengua Tagala (1703).
claims.quote: — Fray Domingo de los Santos, Vocabulario de Lengua Tagala (1703)

claims.statement: Manananggal (1927), directed by José Nepomuceno, was the first Filipino horror film, a silent film with Mary Walter as the manananggal.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal (1927) karya José Nepomuceno adalah film horor Filipina pertama, film bisu dengan Mary Walter sebagai manananggal.
claims.quote: Manananggal (1927), directed by José Nepomuceno, was the first-ever Filipino horror film. It is a silent film starring Mary Walter portraying the manananggal in its current form, with the upper torso detaching.

claims.statement: In 1984 Regal Films released the first Shake, Rattle & Roll, and its Manananggal segment became the franchise's most popular.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1984 Regal Films merilis Shake, Rattle & Roll pertama, dan segmen Manananggal menjadi segmen paling populer dalam waralaba itu.
claims.quote: Back in 1984, Regal Films released the first of the Shake, Rattle & Roll anthology series. The segment Manananggal not only became the most popular segment in the franchise

claims.statement: In the segment, his grandmother tasks Douglas with killing the creature by finding its lower half and stopping it from reattaching.
claims.statement_id: Dalam segmen itu, sang nenek menugaskan Douglas membunuh makhluk itu dengan menemukan tubuh bawahnya dan mencegahnya bersatu kembali.
claims.quote: His grandmother tasks him to kill this creature by locating the lower half and preventing it from re-attaching.

claims.statement: If it fails to recombine before sunrise, the creature is believed to die.
claims.statement_id: Bila tidak bersatu kembali sebelum matahari terbit, makhluk itu dipercaya mati.
claims.quote: If it fails to recombine before sunrise, the creature is believed to die.

claims.statement: The manananggal was hypothesized to explain sudden miscarriages in ancient Philippines.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal pernah diduga menjadi penjelasan atas keguguran mendadak di Filipina kuno.
claims.quote: It was hypothesized to explained sudden ... in ancient Philippines.

claims.statement: The magtatangal account is from Fr. Juan de Plasencia, Customs of the Tagalogs (1589).
claims.statement_id: Catatan tentang magtatangal berasal dari Fr. Juan de Plasencia, Customs of the Tagalogs (1589).
claims.quote: — Fr. Juan de Plasencia, Customs of the Tagalogs (1589)

claims.statement: The manananggal is generally associated with traits similar to other folkloric beings such as vampires, Visayan entities and aswangs.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal umumnya dikaitkan dengan ciri yang mirip makhluk folklor lain seperti vampir, makhluk folklor Visayas, dan aswang.
claims.quote: it is generally associated with characteristics similar to those found in other folkloric beings such as vampires, Visayan folklore entities, and aswangs

claims.statement: In one episode of Shake, Rattle & Roll (1984), directed by Peque Gallaga, Herbert Bautista plays a teenager in a remote province.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu episode Shake, Rattle & Roll (1984) garapan Peque Gallaga, Herbert Bautista memerankan remaja di provinsi terpencil.
claims.quote: In one episode, directed by Peque Gallaga, Herbert Bautista plays a teenager in a faraway province.

claims.statement: Nang Tani (นางตานี, 'Lady of Tani') is a female spirit of Thai folklore; by tradition this ghost appears as a young woman haunting wild banana trees called kluai tani.
claims.statement_id: Nang Tani (นางตานี, 'Nona dari Tani') adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Thailand; menurut tradisi, hantu ini tampil sebagai perempuan muda yang menghuni pohon pisang liar yang disebut kluai tani.
claims.quote: Nang Tani (Thai: นางตานี; "Lady of Tani") is a female spirit of the Thai folklore. According to folk tradition, this ghost appears as a young woman that haunts wild banana trees (Musa acuminata), known in Thai language as Kluai Tani (กล้วยตานี).

claims.statement: Nang Tani belongs to the tree-related female ghosts or fairies called nang mai; similar spirits exist in Cambodian and Lao tradition.
claims.statement_id: Nang Tani termasuk golongan hantu atau peri perempuan penghuni pohon yang disebut nang mai; roh serupa ada dalam cerita rakyat Kamboja dan Laos.
claims.quote: Nang Tani belongs to a type of female ghosts or fairies related to trees known generically as Nang Mai (นางไม้; "Lady of the Wood") in the Thai lore. There is a similar spirit in the Cambodian folklore, as well as in the Lao popular tradition.

claims.statement: Nang Tani is also called Phi Tani ('Ghost of Tani') or Phrai Tani ('Nymph of Tani').
claims.statement_id: Nang Tani juga disebut Phi Tani ('Hantu Tani') atau Phrai Tani ('Peri Tani').
claims.quote: Nang Tani may also be called Phi Tani (ผีตานี; "Ghost of Tani") or Phrai Tani (พรายตานี; "Nymph of Tani").

claims.statement: This ghost dwells in wild banana clumps and is pictured as a beautiful young woman in green Thai dress; she usually hides but comes out and is seen especially on full-moon nights.
claims.statement_id: Hantu ini menghuni rumpun pisang liar dan digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda cantik berbusana tradisional Thai hijau; ia biasanya bersembunyi, tetapi keluar dan terlihat terutama pada malam purnama.
claims.quote: This ghost inhabits the clumps of wild banana trees and is popularly represented as a beautiful young woman wearing a green traditional Thai costume. Most of the time Phi Tani remains hidden, but she comes out of the tree and becomes visible especially on full moon nights.

claims.statement: Her skin is greenish, blending with the tree, her lips red like ripe ivy gourd, her hair black, thick and loose, and her feet hover slightly above the ground.
claims.statement_id: Kulitnya kehijauan menyatu dengan pohon, bibirnya merah seperti buah pepasan masak, rambutnya hitam lebat terurai, dan kakinya melayang sedikit di atas tanah.
claims.quote: She has a greenish complexion, blending with the tree, but her lips have the red color of the ripe ivy gourd. Her hair is black, abundant and untied. She generally appears in a standing position and her feet don't touch the ground, but hover slightly above it.

claims.statement: Cutting trees from Tani's clump is a bad omen; people offer sweets, incense and flowers, and tie coloured satin around the trunk.
claims.statement_id: Menebang pohon dari rumpun yang dihuni Tani dianggap pertanda buruk; orang memberinya kue manis, dupa, dan bunga, serta mengikatkan kain satin berwarna pada batang pohonnya.
claims.quote: It is considered a bad omen to cut trees from the clump Tani inhabits. Offerings are made to her in the form of sweets, incense sticks and flowers. People also often tie a length of colored satin cloth around the trunk of the banana tree believed to be haunted by her.

claims.statement: Because of the ghostly link, people avoid growing it near homes; clumps are often at village outskirts or at the edge of fields by the road.
claims.statement_id: Karena kaitannya dengan hantu, orang tidak mau pohon ini tumbuh dekat rumah; rumpunnya sering ada di pinggir desa atau di tepi ladang dekat jalan.
claims.quote: Owing to their connection with ghosts, people prefer not to have them growing near their homes and they are not found within village compounds. However, clumps of this tree are found not far from inhabited areas, often at the outskirts of villages or at the edge of cultivated fields by the roadside.

claims.statement: Thai oral legend says this spirit may harm men, especially those who wronged women, but she is mostly seen as benevolent and may give food to passing monks.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lisan Thai menyebut roh ini dapat mencelakai laki-laki, terutama yang menyakiti perempuan, tetapi umumnya ia dianggap baik hati dan dapat memberi makanan kepada biksu yang lewat.
claims.quote: Legends of the Thai oral tradition say that this spirit may harm men, especially those who have wronged women, but she is mostly considered benevolent. Nang Tani generally has a gentle disposition and may give food to passing Buddhist monks.

claims.statement: Amulets featuring Nang Tani are popular and come in many shapes and sizes.
claims.statement_id: Jimat bergambar Nang Tani populer dan tersedia dalam berbagai bentuk dan ukuran.
claims.quote: Amulets featuring Nang Tani are popular and come in a variety of shapes and sizes.

claims.statement: Tani also appeared in a Sylvania light bulb commercial for Thai audiences.
claims.statement_id: Tani juga muncul dalam iklan bola lampu Sylvania untuk pemirsa Thailand.
claims.quote: Tani appeared as well in a Sylvania light bulb commercial for Thai audiences.

claims.statement: Bashōnosei, Japanese ghostly banana trees, are listed as a similar ghost; they usually appear as a human face among banana leaves.
claims.statement_id: Bashōnosei, pohon pisang berhantu dari Jepang, disebut sebagai hantu serupa; biasanya tampak sebagai wajah manusia di antara daun pisang.
claims.quote: Bashōnosei: Japanese ghostly banana trees (Musa basjoo), they usually appear as a human face amongst the broad, flat banana leaves.

claims.statement: Nang Tani features in Thai films such as Nang Phrai Tani (1967), which has become a classic.
claims.statement_id: Nang Tani muncul dalam film Thai seperti Nang Phrai Tani (1967), yang telah menjadi klasik.
claims.quote: Nang Tani is a popular folk spirit that has been featured in some Thai films such as Nang Phrai Tani (นางพรายตานี), a film made in 1967 that has become a classic.

claims.statement: The 2000 film Phrai Tani is among lesser films with the banana-tree ghost in the main role.
claims.statement_id: Film Phrai Tani (2000) termasuk film yang kurang penting dengan hantu pohon pisang sebagai tokoh utama.
claims.quote: and 2000 film Phrai Tani (พรายตานี), are less important movies in which the banana tree ghost plays the main role.

claims.statement: The penanggalan or penanggal is a nocturnal vampiric being of Malay ghost lore, a floating woman's head with organs and entrails trailing from the neck; from afar it twinkles like a ball of flame.
claims.statement_id: Penanggalan atau penanggal adalah makhluk malam pengisap darah dari mitos hantu Melayu, berwujud kepala perempuan melayang dengan organ dan isi perut terjuntai dari leher; dari jauh ia berkelip seperti bola api.
claims.quote: The penanggalan or penanggal is a nocturnal vampiric entity from Malay ghost myths. It takes the form of a floating disembodied woman's head, with its organs and entrails trailing from its neck. From afar, the penanggalan is said to twinkle like a ball of flame

claims.statement: Besides the penanggalan there are the Ahp in Cambodia, Kasu in Laos, Krasue in Thailand, Kuyang, Leyak and (in the same sentence) the Manananggal in the Philippines.
claims.statement_id: Selain penanggalan, ada Ahp di Kamboja, Kasu di Laos, Krasue di Thailand, Kuyang, Leyak, dan (menurut kalimat yang sama) Manananggal di Filipina.
claims.quote: Alongside the penanggalan, there is the Ahp (Khmer: អាប) in Cambodia; the Kasu (Lao: ກະສື, pronounced [ka.sɯ̌ː]) in Laos; the Krasue (Thai: กระสือ, pronounced [krā.sɯ̌ː]) in Thailand and much of Southeast Asia; the Kuyang (pronounced [ku.jaŋ]), Leyak

claims.statement: The name penanggalan derives from tanggal, meaning to remove or take off.
claims.statement_id: Nama penanggalan berasal dari kata tanggal, yang berarti melepas atau mencopot.
claims.quote: The name penanggalan derives from the word tanggal, meaning "to remove or take off"

claims.statement: The penanggalan is a witch who gained that form through meditation in a vinegar vat, and by day is a living human.
claims.statement_id: Penanggalan adalah penyihir yang memperoleh wujud itu melalui semadi dalam tong cuka, dan pada siang hari ia manusia hidup biasa.
claims.quote: Rather, it is a witch that developed the ability to take such a form through meditation in a vat of vinegar. The creature is, for all intents and purposes, a living human being during daytime or at any time when it does not detach itself from its body.

claims.statement: In Malaysian folklore, penanggal are mortal women practising black magic; to become one, a woman meditates in a vinegar bath with all but her head submerged.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Malaysia, penanggal adalah perempuan fana yang mengamalkan ilmu hitam; untuk menjadi penanggal, seorang perempuan bersemadi dalam rendaman cuka dengan seluruh tubuh terendam kecuali kepala.
claims.quote: In Malaysian folklore, penanggal are mortal women who practice black magic. To become a penanggal, a woman must meditate during a ritual bath in vinegar, with her whole body submerged except for the head.

claims.statement: The penanggal is also mentioned in the Hikayat Abdullah, written in 1845.
claims.statement_id: Penanggal juga disebut dalam Hikayat Abdullah yang ditulis pada 1845.
claims.quote: The penanggal was also mentioned in Hikayat Abdullah, written in 1845

claims.statement: Those whose blood the penanggalan drinks contract an almost always fatal wasting disease, and anyone brushed by its dripping entrails suffers painful open sores.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang darahnya diisap penanggalan terkena penyakit yang hampir pasti mematikan, dan yang tersentuh tetesan isi perutnya menderita luka terbuka yang menyakitkan.
claims.quote: Those whose blood the penanggalan feeds on contract a wasting disease that is almost inescapably fatal. Furthermore, even if the penanggalan is not successful in her attempt to feed, anyone who is brushed by the dripping entrails will suffer painful open sores

claims.statement: As traditional Malay houses stood on stilts, the penanggal hid beneath them and lapped up a new mother's blood with its long tongue.
claims.statement_id: Karena rumah Melayu tradisional berupa rumah panggung, penanggal bersembunyi di kolongnya dan menjilat darah ibu yang baru melahirkan dengan lidah panjangnya.
claims.quote: As traditional Malay dwellings were stilt houses, the penanggal would hide under the stilts of the house and use its long tongue to lap up the blood of the new mother.

claims.statement: The most common protection is scattering the thorny leaves of the mengkuang plant.
claims.statement_id: Penangkal paling umum adalah menebarkan daun berduri tanaman mengkuang.
claims.quote: The most common protection against a penanggal attack is to scatter the thorny leaves of any of the subspecies of a local plant known as mengkuang

claims.statement: At houses where a birth occurs, jeruju leaves are hung at doors and windows or thorns placed wherever there is blood, lest the penanggalan come to suck it.
claims.statement_id: Di rumah tempat ada kelahiran, biasa digantung daun jeruju di pintu dan jendela atau ditaruh duri di tempat ada darah, agar penanggalan tidak datang mengisapnya.
claims.quote: For this reason it is customary at all houses where a birth occurs to hang up jeruju11 leaves at the doors and windows, or to place thorns wherever there is any blood, lest the penanggalan should come and suck it

claims.statement: It is said a penanggalan came at midnight to suck a man's blood, its intestines caught on thorns by the hedge, and it stayed until daylight, when people saw and killed her.
claims.statement_id: Konon seekor penanggalan datang tengah malam untuk mengisap darah seorang laki-laki, ususnya tersangkut duri dekat pagar, dan ia terjebak sampai pagi, lalu orang melihat dan membunuhnya.
claims.quote: It is said that a penanggalan once came to a man’s house in the middle of the night to suck his blood, and her intestines were caught in some thorns near the hedge, and she had to remain there until daylight, when the people saw and killed her.

claims.statement: Abdullah drew a woman's head and neck with hanging intestines; Mr. M. had it engraved on wood and published in the Anglo-Chinese Gleaner.
claims.statement_id: Abdullah menggambar kepala dan leher perempuan dengan usus terjuntai; Mr. M. menyuruh seorang Tionghoa mengukirnya di kayu dan menerbitkannya dalam Anglo-Chinese Gleaner.
claims.quote: I then drew a picture representing a woman’s head and neck only, with the intestines hanging down. Mr. M. caused this to be engraved on wood by a Chinese, and inserted it with the story belonging to it in a publication called the Anglo-Chinese Gleaner.

claims.statement: Abdullah wrote that this was the penanggalan story he heard from his forefathers, but he did not believe it at all.
claims.statement_id: Abdullah menulis bahwa itulah kisah penanggalan yang ia dengar dari leluhurnya, tetapi ia sama sekali tidak memercayainya.
claims.quote: Such is the story of the penanggalan as I have heard it from my forefathers but I do not believe it in the least.

claims.statement: Singapore penanggalan stories date back to 1912 but have probably existed longer.
claims.statement_id: Kisah penanggalan di Singapura berasal dari 1912, tetapi mungkin sudah ada lebih lama.
claims.quote: Stories of the penanggalan date back to 1912 but have probably been around for longer.

claims.statement: As an extra precaution, a pregnant woman can keep scissors or betel cutters under her pillow, as the penanggalan fears them.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai tambahan, perempuan hamil dapat menyimpan gunting atau kacip pinang di bawah bantal karena penanggalan takut benda itu.
claims.quote: As an extra precaution, the pregnant woman can keep scissors or betel nut cutters under her pillow, as the penanggalan is afraid of these items.

claims.statement: Modern urban legends offer other views of the penanggal, such as a curse or a broken demonic pact.
claims.statement_id: Legenda urban modern menawarkan pandangan lain tentang penanggal, misalnya akibat kutukan atau pelanggaran perjanjian dengan setan.
claims.quote: Modern urban legends offer alternative views of the penanggal. This includes being the result of a curse, or the breaking of a demonic pact.

claims.statement: The Manananggal of the Philippines belongs to the same group.
claims.statement_id: Manananggal di Filipina termasuk kelompok makhluk serupa.
claims.quote: and the Manananggal in the Philippines.

claims.statement: The penanggalan belongs to a group of similar mythological beings known by different names across Southeast Asia.
claims.statement_id: Penanggalan termasuk kelompok makhluk mitologis serupa yang dikenal dengan nama berbeda di berbagai wilayah Asia Tenggara.
claims.quote: The penanggalan belongs to a constellation of similar mythological entities that can be found under different names across different regions of Southeast Asia

claims.statement: According to the Vietnamese creation myth, Âu Cơ (甌姬) was an immortal mountain snow goddess who married Lạc Long Quân and bore an egg sac hatching a hundred children (Bách Việt), ancestors of the Vietnamese; she is honoured as mother of Vietnamese civilization.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos penciptaan bangsa Vietnam, Âu Cơ (甌姬) adalah dewi salju pegunungan yang abadi, menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân, dan melahirkan kantong telur yang menetaskan seratus anak (Bách Việt), leluhur bangsa Vietnam; ia sering dihormati sebagai ibu peradaban Vietnam.
claims.quote: was, according to the creation myth of the Vietnamese people, an immortal mountain snow goddess who married Lạc Long Quân (lit. 'Dragon Lord of Lạc'), and bore an egg sac that hatched a hundred children known collectively as Bách Việt, ancestors to the Vietnamese people. Âu Cơ is often honored as the mother of Vietnamese civilization.

claims.statement: Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) in the snowy mountains who travelled to help the sick, being skilled in medicine and compassionate.
claims.statement_id: Âu Cơ adalah tiên (makhluk abadi) cantik yang tinggal di pegunungan bersalju dan berkelana menolong orang sakit karena mahir pengobatan dan berhati welas asih.
claims.quote: Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) who lived high in the snow-capped mountains. She traveled to help those who suffered from illnesses since she was very skillful in medicine and had a sympathetic heart.

claims.statement: Frightened, Âu Cơ turned into a crane to fly away; Lạc Long Quân, the dragon king from the sea, saw and killed the monster with a rock.
claims.statement_id: Âu Cơ yang ketakutan berubah menjadi bangau untuk terbang menjauh; Lạc Long Quân, raja naga dari laut, melihatnya dan membunuh monster itu dengan batu.
claims.quote: It frightened her, so she transformed into a crane to fly away. Lạc Long Quân, the dragon king from the sea, passed by and saw the crane in danger. He grabbed a nearby rock and killed the monster with it.

claims.statement: They separated, each taking 50 children; Âu Cơ settled in the snowy mountains and raised fifty leaders later known as the Hùng kings (Hùng Vương).
claims.statement_id: Mereka berpisah dengan masing-masing membawa 50 anak; Âu Cơ menetap di pegunungan bersalju dan membesarkan lima puluh pemimpin yang kemudian dikenal sebagai raja-raja Hùng (Hùng Vương).
claims.quote: They separated, each taking 50 children. Âu Cơ settled in the Vietnamese snow-covered mountains where she raised fifty young, intelligent, strong leaders, later known as the Hùng Vương, Hùng kings.

claims.statement: The books Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (15th century) and Lĩnh Nam chích quái (14th century) mention the legend.
claims.statement_id: Kitab Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (abad ke-15) dan Lĩnh Nam chích quái (abad ke-14) menyebut legenda ini.
claims.quote: The books Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (from the 15th century) and Lĩnh Nam chích quái (Wonders plucked from the dust of Linh-nam, from the 14th century) mention the legend.

claims.statement: In the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, Âu Cơ is Đế Lai's daughter.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, Âu Cơ adalah putri Đế Lai.
claims.quote: In Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư Âu Cơ is the daughter of Đế Lai

claims.statement: In the Lĩnh Nam chích quái, Âu Cơ was Đế Lai's concubine before marrying Lạc Long Quân.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Lĩnh Nam chích quái, Âu Cơ adalah selir Đế Lai sebelum menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân.
claims.quote: while in Lĩnh Nam chích quái, Âu Cơ was Đế Lai's concubine before she married off to Lạc Long Quân.

claims.statement: A beautiful fairy named Au Co, living in the mountain, visited the land of Lac Viet to see its beauty.
claims.statement_id: Seorang peri cantik bernama Au Co yang tinggal di gunung mengunjungi negeri Lac Viet untuk melihat keindahannya.
claims.quote: One day, a beautiful fairy named Au Co, who was living in the mountain, visited the country of Lac Viet to see the legendary beauty of the place.

claims.statement: Lạc Long Quân said he was by nature like a dragon in the water and Au Co like a fairy in the mountain; their customs differed, so they must live apart.
claims.statement_id: Lạc Long Quân berkata ia bersifat seperti naga di air dan Au Co seperti peri di gunung; kebiasaan mereka berbeda sehingga harus hidup terpisah.
claims.quote: I am by nature like a dragon in the water, while you are like a fairy in the mountain. Our habits and customs are different. We must live apart from each other.

claims.statement: Because of this legend, the Vietnamese call themselves descendants of the Dragon and Fairy, from one family long ago.
claims.statement_id: Karena legenda ini, orang Vietnam menyebut diri keturunan Naga dan Peri yang berasal dari satu keluarga sejak lama.
claims.quote: Because of this legend, the Vietnamese people refer themselves as the Dragon and Fairy’s descendants who come from the same family a long time ago.

claims.statement: Au Co bore a big bundle rather than an infant; it kept growing and seven days later hatched into a hundred eggs, each revealing a son.
claims.statement_id: Au Co melahirkan buntalan besar, bukan bayi; buntalan itu terus membesar dan tujuh hari kemudian menetas menjadi seratus telur, masing-masing berisi seorang anak laki-laki.
claims.quote: However, Au Co gave birth to a big bundle rather than to an infant. The bundle kept growing. Seven days later, it hatched into one hundred eggs. Each egg then broke open to reveal a bonny son.

claims.statement: The story of Âu Cơ and Lạc Long Quân is widely taught in Vietnamese schools.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Âu Cơ dan Lạc Long Quân diajarkan luas di sekolah-sekolah Vietnam.
claims.quote: The story of Âu Cơ and Lạc Long Quân is taught widely in Vietnamese schools.

claims.statement: In this version, King De Lai and his daughter Au Co from the North visited the South.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, Raja De Lai dan putrinya Au Co dari Utara berkunjung ke Selatan.
claims.quote: At this time, King De Lai and his daughter Au Co from the North went to visit the South.

claims.statement: In the Lĩnh Nam chích quái, Âu Cơ threw her egg sac into a field, thinking it a bad omen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Lĩnh Nam chích quái, Âu Cơ membuang kantong telurnya ke ladang karena mengira membawa pertanda buruk.
claims.quote: Additionally in Lĩnh Nam chích quái, Âu Cơ gave birth to an egg sac but threw it away in the field, believing the egg sac to carry bad omens.
